page.title: Type systems
page.desc: Rules that assign types to expressions and reject programs that misuse them. Static vs dynamic, strong vs weak, nominal vs structural, with inference to reduce annotations.
page.intro: Rules that assign types to expressions and reject programs that misuse them. Static vs dynamic, strong vs weak, nominal vs structural, with inference to reduce annotations.

synapses.text: Static checking happens before running (Rust, Go, TypeScript); dynamic checking at runtime (Python, JavaScript); gradual systems mix them.
Tony Hoare called null references his "billion-dollar mistake" in a 2009 talk; Option types are the remedy.
A signature tells you what a function needs and promises; tooling turns that into completion, refactoring and errors at edit time.

children.title: Generics
children.desc: Parametric polymorphism: writing code once for any type that satisfies a constraint. ML had it in the 1970s; Java added it in 2004, Go in 2022.

children.title: Algebraic data types
children.desc: Product types (structs, tuples) and sum types (enums with payloads, tagged unions). Pattern matching over them makes impossible states unrepresentable.

children.title: Type inference
children.desc: Letting the compiler deduce types from usage. Hindley–Milner (1969/1978) gives ML and Haskell full inference; Rust, TypeScript and Go infer locally.
